# Axial: LLM context

## Product boundary

- `Flow<'env,'error,'value>` is a cold workflow description with explicit dependencies and typed expected failures.
- Axial does not depend on Reified; it binds standard F# `Result` and `Option` directly.
- Use `Flow<'value>`, `Flow<'error,'value>`, `EnvFlow<'env,'value>`, `ExnFlow<'value>`, or
  `ExnEnvFlow<'env,'value>` when the shorter channel combination is sufficient.

## Execution and dependencies

- Pass a record environment and read it with `Flow.envWith`. This is the default and needs no other machinery.
- `Flow.env` is the whole environment; `Flow.envWith f` projects one value out of it. These are ZIO's
  `ZIO.environment` and `ZIO.environmentWith`; a package's `service` accessor is ZIO's `ZIO.service[A]`.
- `Flow.envWith` takes a selector, not a type or a tag: `Flow.envWith _.Clock`. `'env` is an ordinary F# record,
  so there is no type-directed service lookup and no `Flow.service`.
- Declare a per-service contract — an interface `IHasFoo` exposing one member `Foo` — only when a package must ask
  for a service without knowing the caller's record type. Read it through the package's `service` accessor.
- Run with `Flow.run`, `Flow.startTask`, or `Flow.toAsync`; `to*` starts nothing, `start*` begins immediately.
- Use `Layer` plus `Layer.provide` from the separate `Axial.Layers` package only when building the environment is
  itself effectful. Scopes and `acquireRelease` are core and work without layers.
- Use `Flow.fromTask`/`fromAsync` when thrown exceptions are defects; use `attemptTask`/`attemptAsync` when expected
  exceptions belong in the typed failure channel. These take a cancellable factory; `awaitStartedTask` wraps work
  that is already running.
- Use `Bind.error` or `Bind.mapError` only at a `flow {}` bind site where the source error needs immediate assignment.
- Execute finite roots with `App.run`. Use `App.start` when an outer host owns stopping and awaits cleanup.

## Effects and resources

- Process and HttpClient implementations perform only their named `IProcess` or `IHttp` effect. Inject clock,
  randomness, GUID, environment-variable, filesystem, console, and other operational effects explicitly.
- Use `Flow.acquireReleaseWith` for lexical acquire/use/release and `Flow.acquireRelease` or `Layer.acquireRelease` for
  current-scope lifetime.
- Use `Flow.fork`, `join`, and `interrupt` for owned fibers; `forkDetached` states intentional fire-and-forget.
- Use `Schedule.retry` for typed failures, `Schedule.repeat` for successful repetition, `FlowStream` for effectful pull
  streams, and STM for composable transactional coordination.

## Hosts

- `Axial.Hosting` is .NET-only.
- `Axial.Hosting.Node` is Fable JavaScript for Node only.
- `Axial.Hosting.Browser` is Fable JavaScript for browsers only.
- Core Flow is supported in Fable JavaScript on both Node and browsers.

See `/notes/packages-and-platforms.html` for the complete package matrix.
